title: Ultra Messaging Design + Persistence Workshop
answerConvention: For multiple-choice questions, the correct answer is stored at index 0 and options are deterministically shuffled by question ID at render time.

questions.prompt: A subscriber must recover messages published while it was stopped. Which paradigm is required?
questions.explanation: Persistence retains messages and state for recovery after absence or failure.

questions.prompt: Why can changing a source option unexpectedly affect another topic?
options: Both topics may share a transport session whose settings come from the first assigned source
All topics always share one global receiver
questions.explanation: A transport session can carry multiple topics, and several transport-related source options effectively configure that shared session.

questions.prompt: What is the main output of topic resolution for a receiver?
options: Information needed to discover and join the source’s transport session
A persisted copy of every message
A permanent RegID selected by the Store
A quorum vote from Store instances
questions.explanation: Topic resolution connects topic interest to current source and transport-session information.

questions.prompt: Which transport is designed for reliable multicast and scalable fan-out?
questions.explanation: LBT-RM adds reliability to multicast UDP and uses network replication for scalable fan-out.

questions.prompt: Why is transport recovery described as time-bounded?
options: A receiver waits only a configured period before reporting data as unrecoverable
Every retransmission must finish in one CPU tick
Stores delete all messages after one timeout
Topic resolution disables retransmissions after discovery
questions.explanation: If repair cannot complete within configured timing limits, loss becomes application-visible.

questions.prompt: With persistence enabled, how is publisher pacing applied?
options: Transport pacing and persistence pacing are layered
The Store always buffers without limits
questions.explanation: The selected transport has its pacing behavior and persistence adds source-to-Store protection.

questions.prompt: What is the principal performance benefit of source-side batching?
options: It reduces per-message CPU and packet overhead
It persists messages in compressed form
It removes the need for loss recovery
questions.explanation: Batching combines small messages into fewer packets, lowering per-message work.

questions.prompt: During normal Parallel Persistence, where does live message data flow?
options: From the source directly to receivers and in parallel to Stores
From receivers back through the source
questions.explanation: The source transmits to receivers and Stores in parallel.

questions.prompt: Which configuration does a Store process require?
options: Store XML plus LBM configuration for its internal UM objects
questions.explanation: Stores have Store-specific XML and also create UM objects requiring LBM configuration.

questions.prompt: What enables a receiver to register with the correct Store instances?
options: SRI sent by the source over its transport
questions.explanation: SRI carries the Store and source-registration details needed by the receiver.

questions.prompt: What does persistence flight size limit?
options: Messages sent but not yet acknowledged stable by the required persistence condition
The number of topics in a TRD
The number of receiver callback threads
questions.explanation: Flight size bounds outstanding messages awaiting Store stability or retention acknowledgements.

questions.prompt: A topic has ten persistent sources and a 48 MB repository size per source. What is the approximate topic allocation?
options: The source count has no effect
questions.explanation: Repositories are created per topic per source.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes RPP from SPP?
options: RPP can constrain the source based on required receiver consumption
SPP requires every receiver to acknowledge before sending continues
RPP never writes messages to a Store
questions.explanation: Required receiver lag can backpressure an RPP source.

questions.prompt: Why are Session IDs recommended for persistence identity management?
options: They reduce risky direct RegID management and help reconnect durable state safely
questions.explanation: RegIDs are powerful and potentially destructive; Session IDs are the recommended management mechanism.

questions.prompt: When should an application use explicit acknowledgements?
options: When it must align Store consumption with an application-controlled processing/commit boundary
Whenever it wants to disable recovery
questions.explanation: Explicit acknowledgement lets the application define when durable processing is complete.

questions.prompt: Why must a persistent receiver tolerate duplicate delivery?
options: A crash can occur after applying a message but before its durable consumption acknowledgement is recorded
Topic resolution always duplicates every packet
QC requires each Store to deliver a copy to the application
Batching converts one message into two
questions.explanation: Recovery can replay a message whose business effect completed but whose acknowledgement did not.

questions.prompt: How many operational Stores are needed for quorum in a three-Store QC group?
questions.explanation: Quorum is a majority: two of three.

questions.prompt: What should repository thresholds accomplish?
options: Keep normal operation away from the hard size limit while preserving the required recovery window
Force the publisher to hit the limit regularly
questions.explanation: Thresholds and capacity choices should prevent the hard limit from being reached in normal operation.

questions.prompt: When should a UM monitoring approach be selected?
options: Only after the first production incident
questions.explanation: The Concepts Guide recommends deciding the monitoring approach before implementation.

questions.prompt: Which design process is strongest for the final scenario?
options: Derive transport, persistence, recovery, capacity, and monitoring choices from one explicit delivery contract
Choose the fastest transport benchmark and add durability later
Use RPP automatically because it sounds safer
Treat a running Store process as proof of end-to-end health
questions.explanation: A sound UM design aligns every mechanism with the application contract and verifies it through monitoring and failure drills.

exam.selection: Select two of three questions per module. Rotate the selection deterministically on each attempt; focused retries select an alternate question for each weak module.

questions.prompt: A service must deliver data to receivers that start after the source has exited. Which delivery contract fits?
options: Persistence with a Store-backed recovery window
Streaming with a longer topic name
questions.explanation: Transport reliability repairs bounded live-stream loss; persistence is what spans participant absence.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Do not confuse live transport reliability with durable recovery.

questions.prompt: Two topics unexpectedly share a transport-level rate change. What should you inspect first?
options: Whether both sources map to the same transport session and which source configured it first
Whether both receivers have the same RegID
Whether the Store uses disk repositories
questions.explanation: Multiple topics can share a transport session, and session-affecting options may come from the first source assigned.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: A topic is not identical to a transport session.

questions.prompt: Receivers know a topic name but never discover a source. Which plane should be diagnosed first?
options: Topic resolution advertisements, queries, and TRD reachability
questions.explanation: Discovery precedes joining the data transport.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Verify discovery before debugging data or persistence.

questions.prompt: One source must efficiently fan out to hundreds of receivers and multicast is supported. Which starting transport is most appropriate?
options: A Store used as an inline broker
questions.explanation: LBT-RM is UM's reliable multicast transport for scalable fan-out.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Match the transport to topology and fan-out.

questions.prompt: A publisher blocks while the network rate is below its configured limit and the Store is slow to acknowledge writes. What is the leading hypothesis?
options: The persistence flight is full while messages await stability
questions.explanation: Persistence pacing can block independently of the transport rate when stability acknowledgements lag.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Not every blocked send is transport rate control.

questions.prompt: CPU is saturated by 300,000 tiny messages/sec while latency still has headroom. What experiment best fits?
options: Increase intelligent or implicit batching while guarding tail latency
Assign a new RegID for each message
questions.explanation: Batching attacks per-message and per-packet cost; measure its latency effect.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Use a packet-efficiency control for a packet-efficiency problem.

questions.prompt: A design routes every live message source → Store → receiver. What UM persistence property is being missed?
options: Parallel Persistence keeps direct source-to-receiver delivery alongside Store writes
RPP requires an inline Store hop
QC turns Stores into transport routers
questions.explanation: Stores are not normally an inline broker on the live path.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Do not import broker topology assumptions into Parallel Persistence.

questions.prompt: A receiver discovers the topic but cannot register persistently because it lacks Store addresses and source identity. Which control record is missing?
questions.explanation: SRI supplies receiver registration information including Store and source identity details.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Topic discovery alone does not complete persistence registration.

questions.prompt: A topic rule allows 60 MB and twelve active persistent sources publish that topic. What first-order allocation should be planned?
options: About 720 MB before additional overhead and headroom
Unlimited because the Store shares one repository
questions.explanation: The Store creates source repositories per topic per source.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Size per persisted source, not just once per topic.

questions.prompt: A slow analytics consumer must recover later but must never stop the trading publisher. Which default direction best matches?
options: SPP with a recovery window sized for the outage objective
Make the analytics consumer required under RPP
questions.explanation: RPP can make required receiver lag constrain publishing; SPP separates source rate from receiver consumption.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Receiver pacing is not automatically the safer durability choice.

questions.prompt: A receiver writes to a database transactionally. When should it explicitly acknowledge consumption?
options: After the business transaction reaches the chosen durable commit boundary
questions.explanation: The ACK boundary should match the application point from which replay is safe.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Callback delivery is not necessarily completed business processing.

questions.prompt: After restart, a receiver is treated as new and cannot reconnect to its prior durable state. What design area is most suspect?
options: Session ID and RegID lifecycle management
questions.explanation: Durable identity must survive process restart and reconnect the intended Store state.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Process identity is not durable subscription identity.

questions.prompt: A three-Store QC group loses one Store host. What should happen if the remaining Stores are healthy?
options: Messaging can continue with the two-Store majority
All messaging must stop because unanimity is required
The receiver becomes the third Store
questions.explanation: Two of three is a majority quorum.

questions.prompt: A repository repeatedly reaches its hard limit during ordinary bursts. What is the best conclusion?
options: Thresholds, capacity, or the recovery objective are misaligned and require measurement-driven resizing
The hard limit is serving as a healthy steady-state controller
questions.explanation: Normal operation should remain away from the hard limit while preserving the recovery window.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: An emergency capacity boundary is not routine flow control.

questions.prompt: All processes are running, but receiver recovery time is growing past the objective. Which monitoring approach is strongest?
options: Alert on recovery lag/window and correlate Store, flight, ACK, disk, and application signals
questions.explanation: End-to-end contracts require correlated application, UM, Store, and resource signals.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Process liveness is not delivery health.

questions.prompt: Which architecture decision record is complete enough to review?
options: Delivery contract, topology, transport, pacing, persistence mode, identity, recovery, capacity, monitoring, and failure drills
questions.explanation: The design must connect all mechanisms to one delivery contract.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Do not optimize one component without an end-to-end contract.

questions.prompt: A design claims durability because three Store processes run on one host. What review finding is correct?
options: The design lacks host fault-domain independence despite having three processes
Three processes always equal three independent fault domains
QC does not require a majority
Monitoring can compensate for correlated failure
questions.explanation: QC Store instances should be placed on separate physical hosts to tolerate host failure.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Count independent failure domains, not processes.

questions.prompt: Which failure drill best validates the complete durable contract?
options: Crash a receiver after its business commit but before ACK, then verify replay, deduplication, catch-up time, and alerts
questions.explanation: This drill crosses the dangerous acknowledgement boundary and validates recovery plus operations.
questions.misconceptionFeedback: Validate business effects and observability, not only component restart.
